gap: No result ChatGPT got states how long its pick can hold full power. Techtest.org (Michael Barton) measured the Anker Prime 100W A2688 holding 100 W for about an hour before it overheated and throttled. Smartzone measured the same charger dropping to 60 W, below the 65 W this question asks for. The same techtest.org author found the UGREEN Nexode 100W 4-port (CD226) passed his 6-hour constant 100 W test.
standout_why: I compared against three pages. Anker's service page (service.anker.com …a08J1000000XmldIAC) and Anker's US product page give only the maker's split (65 W + 35 W) and no measured figures. The product page says only that temperature is 'monitored 35 times per second'. ComputingForGeeks (rank 13 in chat 2) reprints Mighty Gadget's 65 W + 30 W chart for the UGREEN and says 'These six weren't tested with a USB power meter.' Mighty Gadget's own reviews of both chargers state the splits but measure no per-port watts, temperatures or throttling. None of these has a sustained-load or throttling figure. I could not open the cited ugreen.com/it-it page (HTTP 429), and I did not read thisusb.com, soldermag.com or techgearlab.com.
decides: The finding pulls the pick away from ChatGPT's first answer (Anker A2688) and toward the UGREEN Nexode 100W 4-port. Both makers rate the laptop port at 65 W with a phone attached. Measured under sustained load, though, the Anker throttles: techtest.org gives about 1 hour at 100 W; Smartzone gives a drop to 60 W after its housing reached 55 °C at 10 minutes. The CD226 passed a 6-hour 100 W test. All of these tests were single-port 100 W loads, not a measured 65 W + 35 W split, so the page must say the throttle under a two-device load is inferred, not measured. The same research rules out the Baseus PicoGo Pro AH22 for this page: techtest.org gives its two-port split as 45 W + 45 W, so it falls short of the 65 W line and goes in the 'left out' note. The UGREEN 100W Retractable has no sustained-load test, so its placement rests on the split alone.
